title: React Quiz
description: Fourteen questions covering the whole React tutorial: JSX, components and props, state, events and forms, lists and keys, effects, context, custom hooks, refs, routing, data fetching and performance.

questions.question: What is a React component?
questions.explanation: A component is a plain JavaScript function. It receives props, returns JSX describing the UI, and React calls it whenever its data changes.
options: A CSS class that styles part of the page
A JavaScript function that takes props and returns a description of the UI
An HTML template file loaded by the browser
A server-side script that renders HTML

questions.question: Which command starts the Vite development server in a scaffolded project?
questions.explanation: `npm run dev` runs the `dev` script that create-vite adds to package.json. `npm run build` produces the production bundle in `dist/`.
options: `npm run build`
`npm run dev`
`npm start react`
`vite serve --prod`

questions.question: In JSX, the HTML `class` attribute is written as `___`.
questions.explanation: `class` is a reserved word in JavaScript, so JSX uses `className`; the DOM still receives a normal `class` attribute.

questions.question: Component names must start with a capital letter so that JSX treats them as components rather than HTML tags.
questions.explanation: JSX compiles lowercase tags to DOM elements and capitalized tags to component references. `<card />` creates an unknown HTML element; `<Card />` calls your function.

questions.question: What is `n` after `bump` has been called once?
questions.explanation: Updater functions are queued and applied in order to the latest state: 10 doubled is 20, then plus one is 21.

questions.question: In a submit handler, which call stops the browser from reloading the page?
questions.explanation: `preventDefault()` cancels the event's default action, which for a submit event is navigating to the form's action URL. `stopPropagation()` only affects bubbling.
options: `e.stopPropagation()`
`e.preventDefault()`
`return false`
`e.cancel()`

questions.question: Why is the array index a poor key for a list that can be reordered or filtered?
questions.explanation: Keys give items an identity across renders. When an item's index changes, React pairs its state and DOM node with whichever item now sits at that index.
options: Index keys are slower for React to compare
The index of an item changes, so React matches state and DOM nodes to the wrong items
Indexes are not unique within one list
React does not accept numbers as keys

questions.question: In development, Strict Mode runs an effect, then its cleanup, then the effect again on mount. Why?
questions.explanation: Simulating an unmount and remount reveals effects that leak timers, listeners or requests because their cleanup is missing or wrong. Production builds run effects once.
options: To measure how long the effect takes
To expose effects whose cleanup is missing or incorrect
Because effects always run twice in React
To warm up the browser cache

questions.question: In React 19 you can provide a context by rendering the context object directly with a prop: `<ThemeContext ___={theme}>`.
questions.explanation: The provider prop is `value`. React 19 allows `<ThemeContext value={theme}>`; the older `<ThemeContext.Provider value={theme}>` still works.

questions.question: A custom hook's name must start with `use` so that the lint rules can verify the rules of hooks inside it.
questions.explanation: React does not check the name at runtime, but `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` relies on the prefix, and the convention tells readers the function calls hooks.

questions.question: This component throws "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'focus')". Why?
questions.explanation: Refs are attached after React commits to the DOM. During the first render `inputRef.current` is still `null`. Move the focus call into `useEffect` or an event handler.
options: `useRef` must be called with a DOM element
`inputRef.current` is `null` during render; the node exists only after commit, so focus it in an effect
The `ref` attribute must be set to `inputRef.current`
Inputs cannot receive focus programmatically

questions.question: What does `<NavLink>` add that `<Link>` does not?
questions.explanation: `NavLink` knows whether its destination matches the current URL and adds the `active` class plus `aria-current="page"`, which is what navigation menus need.
options: Prefetching of the target page
An `active` class and `aria-current` when its route matches the URL
A full page reload on click
Support for external URLs

questions.question: In TanStack Query, what is the role of `queryKey`?
questions.explanation: The key is the address of the data in the cache. Components using the same key share one request and one result, and `invalidateQueries` targets data by key.
options: It is the URL that is fetched
It identifies the data in the cache so components can share it and invalidate it
It sets how often the query refetches
It names the React component that renders the data

questions.question: `useMemo(() => compute(a), [a])` calls `compute` again when:
questions.explanation: `useMemo` returns the cached result until a dependency changes. Re-renders caused by other state or by the parent reuse the previous value.
options: The component re-renders for any reason
`a` has changed since the previous render
Never; the value is computed once
A parent component re-renders
